newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 140-155 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 140-155 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 140-155 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 110 bcf to 220 bcf for the week ended January 24.
Traders said the main reason for disparate views was that some factored in economic incentives to pull storage since cash-to-futures spreads were still in steep backwardation.

"This (AGA) should be a relatively high number, not only because of the cold on the East Coast, but because LDCs had every incentive to get rid of gas," said one East Coast trader, noting the 173 bcf, or 19 percent, stock surplus to last year in the East.
In last report, overall stocks dove an unexpectedly-high 262 bcf, moving the total back to slightly below last year. The four week average drawdown is 133 bcf.
For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 161 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would just about erase the slight deficit to last year.

But most agreed eastern eastern storage, which fell by 86 bcf in 1996, would remain at a significant surplus to year-ago. And producing stocks, which dropped by 48 bcf, and western stocks, which fell by 27 bcf, were likely to continue to significantly lag last year's levels, traders said.
